messages:
Alex: Heads up — saw a spike of 503/502s during the us-west spot reclaim window last night. Mostly streaming requests that failed during the final 30s of node preemption.
Mina: ugh, saw those alerts. latency SLOs got clobbered for a few routes. any root cause yet?
Alex: looks like a combination: (1) new requests routed to nodes already in drain state, (2) our streaming token cutover currently drops the connection when the node loses GPU, (3) requeue path is synchronous and times out > client TTL so requests fail rather than requeue.
Jordan: can we do a small handshake where the node advertises a DRaining boolean upstream? then router can stop sending new streams and only allowed continue tokens can be proxied.
Sam: agreed. We already have a node annotation in k8s when drain starts. Problem is timing + envoy connection reuse — some streams are sticky to a node. We need a way to signal in-flight streams that they should checkpoint and switch to continuation.
Ryan: proposal: introduce a lightweight Continuation token that is emitted by serving runtime when it receives a SIGTERM/eviction event. Token contains last-kv-offset, batch cursor, and a nonce. Router accepts the token and can reconnect the client to another node using the token to resume. Token TTL 90s, max-retries 2.
Mina: sounds ok. how do we protect against token replay or at-most-once semantics? we need idempotency key in the token and a small dedupe store for 2 minutes.
Alex: yes — token must include request-id and sequence, signed with ephemeral HMAC key rotated per-minute (or use vault/HSM). we already have HMAC machinery in place for signed URLs.
Jordan: also need backpressure: when node enters drain, it should flip a header so router reduces new request routing weight to 0 for streaming routes. That gives time for in-flight streams to emit continuation tokens.
Sam: implementation details: runtime on SIGTERM does: 1) set pod annotation draining=true 2) stop accepting new sessions 3) flush KV cache to checkpoint blobstore 4) return continuation token in-stream
Sam: example header: ```X-Continuation: eyJpZCI6IjEyMyIsIm9mZnNldCI6NTAwLCJuYmYiOjE2fQ==``` and client reconnect uses: ```POST /resume  Headers: X-Continuation: <token> X-Request-Id: <id>```
Mina: routing changes: router needs to treat resume as a first-class operation, map token -> node-state, and prefer reserved-capacity pool if token validation fails to avoid user-facing failure. But that has cost implications.
Alex: cost tradeoff: fallback to reserved on resume only (not for initial request) — small incremental cost but big availability win. We should instrument fallback count and cost burn.
Ryan: requeue logic: make requeue asynchronous and push to a lightweight queue with 2s backoff jitter. If queue not accepted within 10s, fallback to reserved or return a resumable failure to client.
Jordan: what about KV cache consistency? If we checkpoint on drain and resume on another node, we need to ensure the resumed node can lazily pull the checkpoint; keep checkpoint TTL 5m and keep it in hot store (s3+warm cache).
Sam: operational runbook additions: add alert for continuation-token-generation rate and resume-fallback-rate. playbook step: if resume-fallback spikes > 5% for 10m, remove spot pool from routing until patched.
Alex: testing plan: canary small percent of traffic with continuation enabled behind a feature flag. will add synthetic traffic that triggers evictions and measure end-to-end resume success and SLO impact.
Mina: security note: tokens must be short-lived + signed + audience-limited. add token metrics for expired, replay, invalid signatures.
eviction-bot: eviction event recorded: node gpunode-7 triggered preemptible_reclaim at 1987649800; continuation-token emit simulated by runtime v2.4.3-canary.
Ryan: questions: TTL/tries numbers: everyone ok with TTL 90s / 2 retries / checkpoint TTL 5m?
Jordan: +1 for TTL/2 tries. 90s keeps requeues bounded and fits typical client reconnect windows.
Mina: +1. we should limit resume-fallback to reserved to X reqs/min per-customer to control cost.
Alex: action items: @Ryan proto token format + HMAC spec; @Sam runtime SIGTERM flow + code changes; @Mina router + rate-limits; @Jordan S3 checkpoint lifecycle; @Alex will draft monitoring panels and runbook. target PRs by EOW.
Sam: I'll open runtime PR with comments and smoke tests.
Mina: I'll prototype router weighted drain and resume routing in the same branch so we can integrate quickly.
Alex: thanks team. I'll post links to design doc and the canary plan once PRs land. :thumbsup:
